main_text.p: usuvenit, idem in rebus existimamus usuvenire. Quando ait Philosophus, non bis ex eo quòd verba rerum notæ ha-bentur, videri quicquid verbis acci-dat, idem rebus ipsis contingere: summam probabilitatem ac verisimilitu-dinem eius insinuare voluit. quæ quidem in Eucharistiæ causa nonnullis tanta est, vt in hoc vnico fundamento infistere, eóque aut vincere aut cadere cogitent: alij perspicuitatem, alij feriam asseuerationè verborum Christi in Cœna: alij quòd non sit historica narratio, aut parabolica concio, vt multæ aliæ in scriptura sacra reperiũ-tur: sed in vltimo penè agone expres-sa oratio: & quid non præterea, obte-dunt. Semper tamen eòdem redit res, vt propterea quia verba notæ rerum sunt, idem in rebus, quod in verbis u-suvenit, usuvenire credatur. Cæterũ multos hac ratione decipi, Aristote-les pulchra comparatione ostendit, paulòpòst subiiciens, ὥσπερ οἱ μὴ δεινοὶ τὰς ψήφους φέρειν, [illegible, ~12 letters]

page.notes: The first word is a fragment continuing from the previous page, so it is printed as "usuvenit" after the cut-off "verbis" line, which lies in the cut-off left edge. The final Greek clause is partly illegible in the scan. The paragraph runs unbroken from the top of the page to the Greek line; no paragraph break is visible. The page number reads "13" in old-style figures.
